## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Gemma4-12B quantized at 4-bit occupies ~7.8 GB VRAM, leaving 8.2 GB headroom in a 16GB VRAM pool for up to 32k token KV cache and activation workspaces. (high confidence) — https://github.com/google/gemma_pytorch · keywords: Gemma4-12B Cross-Platform Residency and Benchmarking · also: https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad
- [statement] When running completely resident in RTX 5080 GDDR7 VRAM (~1000 GB/s), Gemma4-12B generates ~85-92 tokens per second, roughly double the ~42-45 tokens per second achieved on Apple Silicon M5 Max (~400 GB/s). (high confidence) — https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad · keywords: Gemma4-12B Cross-Platform Residency and Benchmarking · also: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Serving Gemma4-12B via Ollama Metal introduces a 10-15% throughput penalty compared to native MLX-LM due to runtime translation and generic Metal kernel dispatch in ggml. (high confidence) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples · keywords: Gemma4-12B Cross-Platform Residency and Benchmarking · also: https://github.com/google/gemma_pytorch

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Pre-allocation of static tensor workspaces in Tinygrad or TensorRT avoids CUDA and Metal memory fragmentation during extended generation passes. (high confidence) — https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad · keywords: Gemma4-12B Cross-Platform Residency and Benchmarking · also: https://github.com/google/gemma_pytorch
